subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is an endothermic process?
questions.explain: Thermal decomposition takes in energy from the surroundings, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: An advantage of a hydrogen fuel cell over a petrol engine is that it:
options: Produces only water as a product
Stores more energy than any battery
questions.explain: Fuel cells produce only water, so they release no carbon dioxide at the point of use.

questions.q: Why does a reaction generally slow down over time even without changing conditions?
options: The reactant concentration decreases as it is used up
questions.explain: As reactants are consumed, their concentration falls, so collisions are less frequent and the rate decreases.

questions.q: Is bond making endothermic or exothermic?
questions.explain: Forming new bonds releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: In a hydrogen fuel cell, hydrogen and oxygen combine to produce:
questions.explain: A hydrogen fuel cell produces only water (and electrical energy) as hydrogen reacts with oxygen.

questions.q: Is bond breaking endothermic or exothermic?
questions.explain: Breaking bonds requires energy to be supplied, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: On a reaction profile, the activation energy is:
options: The energy difference between reactants and products
The energy of the products only
The minimum energy needed to start the reaction
questions.explain: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for reactant particles to react, shown as the hump on the profile.

questions.explain: Combustion releases energy to the surroundings, making it exothermic.

questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium in a closed system:
options: The forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate
All reactants have been used up
questions.explain: At equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an exothermic process?
options: Neutralisation of an acid and alkali
questions.explain: Neutralisation releases energy, so the temperature of the mixture rises — it is exothermic.

questions.q: According to collision theory, for a reaction to occur particles must collide and have at least what?
questions.explain: Particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy to react.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of a reaction?
options: Increasing the surface area of a solid reactant
questions.explain: A larger surface area gives more sites for collisions, increasing the rate.
